body.rationale: IPS status: the run header gives it as ratified, and the reviews treat the breaches as real. I rank on hard-limit compliance and covariance-based robustness, with the four families kept in view. 1) cvar_minimization: no hard breaches, the best backtest Sharpe among compliant names (0.74) and a -18.7% drawdown. Its intra-category reviewer found the optimiser working as designed. The weakness, volatility tuned to exactly 8.00% and 2.9 effective assets, is real but bounded. 2) black_litterman: compliant, with a -21.9% drawdown and 3.28% tracking error. Reviewers flagged the double-counted ETF AUM prior and the reliance on stock-bond hedging, but the execution reconciles. 3) resampled_efficient_frontier: compliant with 13.1 effective assets, and resampling tempers return-forecast noise. Its -24.84% drawdown sits only 16bp inside the limit, which keeps it below black_litterman. 4) inverse_volatility: compliant and transparent, with 14.8 effective assets. It ignores correlation, and the roughly 43% in credit sleeves that fall together is a real concern, but it breaches no limit. 5) risk_parity: the most covariance-driven of the field, which suits the late-cycle regime evidence in section 4.3. Its only breach is a small volatility shortfall (7.56% vs the 8% floor), and reviewers found the effective-N-as-risk-dispersion claim overstated. Why 1 beats 5: cvar_minimization clears every IPS limit with the lowest drawdown and the highest backtest Sharpe of the compliant set, whereas risk_parity breaches the volatility floor, has a weaker backtest Sharpe (0.57), and offers no risk-contribution output to verify its core claim. These five span non_traditional, return_optimized, heuristic and risk_structured. Bottom flag: market_cap_weight breaches two hard limits, with a -40.6% drawdown that the CRO treats as a floor and a CRO risk score of 0.80, the worst in the field. Reviewers showed the weights are ETF AUM rather than a market portfolio, with about 77% in equity, and the proposal itself calls it a diagnostic, not a recommendation. I did not flag pc_researcher or others, because diversifiers orthogonal to consensus, including my own, have ensemble value and should not be flagged reflexively.
